value: twigs bearing sawfly (Diprion pini) eggs released volatiles that attracted the egg parasitoid Chrysonotomyia ruforum; jasmonic acid treatment also induced attractive volatiles
method: olfactometer choice tests of parasitoid females (22-30 per treatment) with egg-laden, egg-free and jasmonic acid treated pine twigs
conditions: laboratory olfactometer, cut twigs and needles of Scots pine

source.authors: Monika Hilker, Carsten Kobs, Martti Varama, Kai Schrank
source.title: Insect egg deposition induces Pinus sylvestris to attract egg parasitoids

where: Results, first paragraph (Silverchair copy of the journal article opened through WebFetch)
quote: The egg parasitoid C. ruforum was attracted by volatiles emitted from pine needles laden with eggs of the sawfly D. pini.
note: Egg deposition as the cue and a systemic response in needles near egg-laden ones are reported; the page copy carried no author list, so authors, year and journal come from the Crossref record on main's wanted list (harvest-c13). Twigs were cut for the olfactometer, but the induced volatile response is that of a living plant to a herbivore cue (owner reading 10(a)).

value: methyl jasmonate sprayed on seedlings raised (-)-beta-pinene in phloem, yet total monoterpene content of basal phloem did not rise
method: seedlings sprayed with 5, 10 or 25 mM emulsified methyl jasmonate in 2.5% ethanol; monoterpene content of phloem and needles analysed, Scots pine and Norway spruce compared

source.authors: Lina Lundborg, Göran Nordlander, Niklas Björklund, Henrik Nordenhem, Anna-Karin Borg-Karlson
source.title: Methyl Jasmonate-Induced Monoterpenes in Scots Pine and Norway Spruce Tissues Affect Pine Weevil Orientation

where: Discussion (PMC full text opened through WebFetch)
quote: For P. sylvestris, the MeJA treatment did not induce an increase of the total monoterpene contents of the basal phloem.
